subject: Invoice batching & portal fallback process for new vendors
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@kestrel-supplies.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
Cc: accounts-payable@kestrel-supplies.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: New vendor onboarding — invoice batches vs single emails

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — Kestrel is onboarding with Redwood next week and I have a couple of operational questions from our AP team. We usually send one consolidated invoice per customer per week (one CSV/ZIP containing multiple POs and line items). Other customers we work with want us to send individual PDF invoices against each PO.

Before we finish our vendor setup, can you confirm:
- Does Redwood accept batched invoice uploads (CSV/ZIP) through the portal and reconcile multiple POs in one file?
- If we fall back to email (accounts-payable@redwood.example.com), do you have a preferred subject convention or file naming pattern so your AP can auto-route?
- Any mandatory fields you require in a compact CSV? We try to keep the payload minimal: PO number, invoice number, invoice date, net amount, tax, currency.

Happy to share a sample CSV and the vendor onboarding form — attaching both.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations
Kestrel Supplies

Attachments: kestrel_weekly_sample.zip (csv inside), onboarding_questions.docx

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@kestrel-supplies.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.example.com, jordan_blake@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — invoice batches vs single emails

Hi Samantha — great to meet you and welcome aboard. Quick answers up front, followed by a couple of notes: 

- Portal (preferred): Yes, the portal supports a batched CSV/ZIP upload that can contain multiple invoices across multiple POs. Our ingestion pipeline will parse each line and attempt PO matching. The portal has a 50MB file size limit and we recommend batching by week or by ship-date to avoid very large files.

- Email fallback: We do accept invoice email fallback to accounts-payable@redwood.example.com but require a strict subject filename convention to help automated routing. Preferred subject: "Invoice: <VendorName> | <YYYYMMDD> | BATCH-<batch-id>". For file names: "<VendorName>_Invoices_<YYYYMMDD>_BATCH-<id>.zip". If you include a simple manifest.csv in the zip with line-level PO mapping it speeds ingestion.

- Minimal CSV fields we require: PO, invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), line_description, qty, unit_amount, tax_amount, currency, total_amount. Optional: vendor_reference, cost_center. If a field is missing we will attempt best-effort inference but that increases manual exceptions.

Attached: redwood_onboarding_form_v2.pdf (please fill and sign) and a compact_invoice_sample.csv.

Next steps: if you can return the onboarding form and a signed W-9 (or equivalent) we can provision your vendor account and enable portal access. If you expect >100 invoices/month and prefer batching, tell us your weekly file size and estimated line count so we can preconfigure ingestion throughput.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Vendor Enablement Manager
Redwood Inference

Grace / Jordan — quick internal note before we finalize the reply to Kestrel. Two operational items to confirm: 

1) PO lifecycle: If a vendor sends a batched CSV referencing open POs, our matching logic will apply payments to the earliest-matching PO by PO number and date. We need to confirm whether we should support "apply to multiple POs by manifest mapping" (we do if the manifest explicitly lists PO->invoice lines). Monica suggests making manifest mandatory for batches >25 lines to avoid misallocations.

2) Exception handling: For parsed lines with ambiguous matches or missing currency, our portal will create an "AP exception" ticket and email ap-ops@redwood.example.com. Shall we add a short escalation note in the onboarding form instructing vendors to include contact and timezone for faster resolution?

I recommend we: (a) make the manifest strongly recommended for batches >25 lines and mandatory for batches >250 lines, (b) add a line in the onboarding form about preferred contact for exception triage.

If you both agree I'll add those fields to redwood_onboarding_form_v2.pdf and send an updated copy.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Manager, Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: New vendor onboarding — invoice batches vs single emails

Samantha — thanks for the sample file and patience. Short version: portal is best for batching; email fallback is supported with naming conventions and a manifest to speed routing. A few operational bullets so your AP team can implement immediately: 

- Preferred portal file cadence: weekly (one file per week) or daily if you have frequent shipments.
- Manifest: strongly recommended for >25 lines; mandatory for >250 lines. Manifest fields: invoice_number, invoice_date, PO, line_id, line_amount.
- Subject convention for email fallback: exactly "Invoice: Kestrel Supplies | YYYYMMDD | BATCH-<id>". We will not ingest files that do not follow the subject pattern automatically; they will create an AP exception.
- Minimal CSV columns: PO, invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), line_description, qty, unit_amount, tax_amount, currency, total_amount. No merged cells or PDF-embedded CSVs.
- Exceptions: missing currency or ambiguous PO creates AP exception; include a contact and timezone on the onboarding form so we can triage.

I've attached the onboarding form and a compact sample. Please return the completed onboarding_form and a W-9 (or local tax equivalent) and we'll flip portal access the same business day. If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute walkthrough with our AP operations team to review sample files and manifest layout.

Best,
Grace
Vendor Enablement Manager
Redwood Inference
